text.p: These are the leading stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Monday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- SERBIA -
POLITIKA

- Final list of participants at the round table on Kosovo to be held in New York was still not finalised a day ahead of the scheduled start of the talks Monday. The ruling Socialist Party of Serbia, which will not participate in the talks, accepts dialogue on the issue but inside the country.
- Yugoslav ambassador to Croatia Veljko Knezevic visits Eastern Slavonia, urges Serbs to stay and vote in large numbers at the upcoming local elections which is in their own best interest.

- Price of Yugoslav foreign debt grows to 51-53 cents to the dollar based on encouraging forecasts on increase of its exports and its hard currency reserves made by Merril Lynch bank at the recent European financial convention organised in London by the European Union.
- Out of 130,000 tonnes of imported wheat Yugoslavia bought 100,000 from Germany.
- The Serbian draft law on concessions to provide new ways of securing fresh foreign capital, says chairman of the management board of the Serbian power company Elektroprivreda Srbije Dragan Kostsic.
- There are 776,697 unemployed in Serbia or 5.8 percent more than in the same period last year, according to official statistics.
- Kosovo will always be an integral part of Serbia but the republic should draw up a special programme and earmark funds for its development, said head of the Kosovo district Milos Nesovic.
NASA BORBA
- Rumours about disputes within opposition coalition Zajedno in Washington are fabricated says Zoran Djindjic, president of the Democratic Party which is one of the coalition partners.
- The Kosovo issue cannot be resolved before a change of power in Serbia, says Bishop Artemije of Raska and Prizren.
- Special ties agreement between Boisnian Serb Republic and Yugoslavia is welcome although it should have been signed much earlier, according to the Bosnian Serb Deputy Prime Minister Aleksa Buha.

- Serbs in Eastern Slavonia held a referendum on whether the area should remain a single administrative unit after its reintegration into Croatia. Many believe that a single area would give them a feeling of security.

- Round table on refugees in Yugoslavia urges international organisations not to stop or decrease humanitarian aid and governments of Yugoslavia and Bosnian Serb republic to secure sources of financing elementary refugee needs.
- Bosnian foreign trade minister Hasan Murataovic calls for speedy conclusion of a customs-free agreement between Yugoslavia and Bosnia.
- Dinar strengthens on black market exchange rate due to shortage of cash and is exchanged for 3.65 German marks.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Preparations underway for annual rehauling of thermal power plant Kostolac for which Serbian Power Company EPS has earmarked 70 million dinars.
- Over 400,000 visitors saw the Belgrade car show and a number of firms managed to sell all exhibited cars, including Mitsubishi, Ford, Peugeot and other big car producers.
- World Bank approved a $55 million loan to Bosnian Serb republic for emergency projects in agriculture, housing, and power.
- Minimum costs for food alone for a four member family in March stood at between 1,440 and 1,480 dinars, while the average wage in February was 941 dinars, according to statistics.
POLITIKA EKSPRES

- Serbian agriculture minister Jovan Babovic says government has repaid in full the cash part of debt to farmers for sugar beet and oil seed. Around 90 percent of barter repayment of farm debt also completed. Pressure on oil and sugar refineries to repay their debts to farmers.
- MONTENEGRO -
POBJEDA
- Pjelvja zinc and lead mine plans to produce 200,000 tonnes of ore this year. It produced 30,232 tonnes in the first three months.
- Montenegro purchases 100 million German marks' worth of cattle products annually.
- UNESCO expected to include National park Biogradska Gora in its natural heritage list. -- Belgrade Newsroom +381 11 2224254
